case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Puffy's, LLC v. Department of Health
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a writ of mandamus compelling the Department of Health to issue a registration certificate, holding that the plain text of its own administrative rule obligated the agency to act and that the applicant had no other adequate remedy.
key_cases.relevance: It gives an audit finding of rule noncompliance a concrete judicial remedy rather than a purely political one.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the text of ARSD 44:90:03:16 obligated the Department to issue the registration certificate to Puffy's, and Puffy's had a clear legal right to receive it.

key_cases.case_name: Mercer v. South Dakota Attorney General Office
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed denial of a public records request for a death investigation file, holding SDCL 1-27-1.5(5) and SDCL 23-5-11 expressly exempt law enforcement investigative reports and confidential criminal justice information, and that no right to redaction or partial release exists.
key_cases.relevance: Audit-style requests for investigative files run into the same SDCL 1-27-1.5(5) exemption this case enforces.
key_cases.quote: The records developed or received by the agencies charged with the duty to investigate Benda's death constitute confidential criminal justice information as defined by statute.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's reasonable efforts requirement creates no privately enforceable right, so beneficiaries cannot sue to enforce it under the Act itself or under 42 U.S.C. 1983.
key_cases.relevance: Federal audit and reimbursement mechanisms are the enforcement channel this decision leaves open.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed and held that a city's confidential construction settlement agreement is a public record open to inspection, because the Public Records Act's presumption of openness and the SDCL 1-27-1.3 directive to construe fiscal records liberally require narrow construction of the SDCL 1-27-1.5(20) exception.
key_cases.relevance: SDCL 1-27-1.3 requires fiscal records, audits, vouchers and expenditure records to be construed liberally in favor of access, which is the statutory hook for any financial audit of South Dakota child-welfare spending.
key_cases.quote: Therefore, in accordance with that presumption of openness and the requirement that we construe the statute liberally in favor of openness, we must narrowly construe the exception with subdivision (20).
